metadata.source: ESPN historical NBA scoreboards; official NBA 2023/24 regular-season standings
metadata.coverage: 1230 completed NBA regular-season games, 30 teams, 160 Eastern calendar game days, 24 October 2023–14 April 2024. Cup group/quarterfinal/semifinal games included; Cup championship, preseason, All-Star, play-in and playoffs excluded. Real final scores and source-reported quarters/overtimes; no player or advanced statistics.

metricDefinitions.points: The league-points field is unused (0). Points for and against sum real final scores, including overtime.
metricDefinitions.difference: Points differential = points scored − points conceded.
metricDefinitions.ranking: Win percentage, then official NBA final regular-season conference rank for ties within a conference. Equal records across conferences are grouped Eastern then Western for display; no official combined NBA seed is implied. Final conference ranks are source-provided, not recalculated for earlier game days.
metricDefinitions.round: Game day is the chronological index of a date with regular-season games in America/New_York. It is not an official NBA round, team game number, or UTC date.
metricDefinitions.series: Cumulative win percentage (0–100) after each Eastern calendar game day; idle teams retain their previous cumulative value.
metricDefinitions.winPct: Wins ÷ played × 100; zero before a team has played.
metricDefinitions.form: Latest five completed results, oldest → newest. W = win; L = loss.
metricDefinitions.splits: Home/away aggregates follow ESPN's designated home and away teams, including neutral-site games.
metricDefinitions.periods: Source-reported quarters followed by any overtime periods. Missing period scores remain absent; none are imputed.
metricDefinitions.missing: Unavailable player and advanced statistics remain absent rather than becoming zero.
metricDefinitions.verification: All 30 teams' wins, losses, total points scored and total points allowed are independently checked against the official NBA regular-season standings API. Conference ranks use PlayoffRank (regular-season position), not PlayoffSeeding (after play-in).
